name: MUSE pivotal
question: Does transurethral alprostadil improve intercourse success compared with placebo in men with organic erectile dysfunction who respond to in-clinic testing?

arms.label: Transurethral alprostadil at the effective in-clinic dose

design.population: Men aged 27 to 88 years with chronic erectile dysfunction from various organic causes who achieved an intercourse-sufficient erection during in-clinic alprostadil testing.

verdictNote: Home efficacy was measured only after a positive in-clinic dose test.
takeaway: Among men with organic erectile dysfunction who responded to in-clinic dosing, transurethral alprostadil led to intercourse at least once during three months more often than placebo (299/461 versus 93/500 home-treatment reporters).

reports.label: Pivotal placebo-controlled report
reports.citation: Padma-Nathan H, Hellstrom WJ, Kaiser FE, et al. "Treatment of men with erectile dysfunction with transurethral alprostadil." *N Engl J Med.* 1997;336(1):1-7. doi:10.1056/NEJM199701023360101
reports.followUp: Three months of randomized home treatment after in-clinic response

results.measure: At least one successful intercourse during three months of home treatment; risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Analyzed among 961 men who reported at least one home treatment. Risk difference calculated from reported proportions; prespecified testing threshold unavailable in abstract.

results.measure: Response to in-clinic dose testing among all enrolled men
results.note: Pre-randomization selection stage; no placebo comparison.

harms.label: Mild penile pain per alprostadil administration
harms.note: Treatment-level denominator and placebo rate were not stated in the abstract.

harms.label: In-clinic hypotension
harms.note: Patient-level numerator and placebo rate were not stated in the abstract.

harms.label: Priapism or penile fibrosis
harms.note: The abstract reports no cases in the trial; a comparator-specific denominator is unavailable.

delivery.label: In-clinic dose testing
delivery.value: Up to four transurethral alprostadil doses (125, 250, 500 and 1000 micrograms) before randomized home treatment at the effective dose.

delivery.label: Intercourse after administrations in responders
delivery.value: On average, 7 of 10 alprostadil administrations were followed by intercourse in men responsive to treatment.

reports.label: Post-prostatectomy subgroup
reports.dateLocator: PubMed PMID 9751346, October 1998 issue; day unavailable
reports.citation: Costabile RA, Spevak M, Fishman IJ, et al. "Efficacy and safety of transurethral alprostadil in patients with erectile dysfunction following radical prostatectomy." *J Urol.* 1998;160(4):1325-1328. doi:10.1016/s0022-5347(01)62527-8
reports.followUp: Three months of home treatment after a positive in-clinic test
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 1326

results.measure: Response among men with radical prostatectomy as an erectile dysfunction cause
results.note: Retrospective subgroup; 726/1127 (64.4%) men with other organic etiologies responded in clinic (P = 0.035).
results.locator: Full text, Results, Clinic phase, p 1326

results.endpoint: Successful intercourse at home after prostatectomy
results.measure: At least one successful intercourse during three months among 263 post-prostatectomy participants reporting home treatment
results.note: Retrospective subgroup; analysis includes 263 home-treatment reporters, not the 243 three-month completers. The 50.6-percentage-point risk difference is calculated from reported patient counts; no confidence interval reported. Among other etiologies, 227/335 (67.8%) active and 84/363 (23.1%) placebo patients reported intercourse.
results.locator: Full text, Results, Home treatment phase, p 1326; Figure 1, p 1327

results.measure: Product of in-clinic response and active-drug home success rates
results.note: Authors' calculated estimate, not a separately observed randomized outcome.
results.locator: Full text, Results, Home treatment phase, p 1326

harms.label: Penile pain during home treatment
harms.locator: Full text, Results, Adverse effects, p 1326; Table 4, p 1327
harms.note: Patient comparison P <0.001; placebo numerator not printed.

harms.label: Urethral pain or burning during home treatment
harms.locator: Full text, Results, Adverse effects, p 1326; Table 4, p 1327
harms.note: Active versus placebo P <0.001. Among other organic etiologies, 35/337 (10.4%) on active drug reported urethral pain or burning (P = 0.027 versus post-prostatectomy).

harms.label: Hypotension during clinic titration
harms.value: 3/384 (0.8%) post-prostatectomy patients versus 47/1127 (4.2%) with other organic etiologies (P <0.001)
harms.locator: Full text, Results, Adverse effects, p 1326; Table 4, p 1327
harms.note: Measured before randomization; comparison is by erectile-dysfunction etiology, not home-treatment assignment.

harms.label: Other adverse effects during home treatment

values.exp: Dizziness 2.4% of 126; no syncope, urinary tract infection, fibrosis, or priapism
values.ctl: Dizziness 0% and urinary tract infection 0.7% of 137; no syncope, fibrosis, or priapism

harms.locator: Full text, Results, Adverse effects, p 1326; Table 4, p 1327
harms.note: Table 4 reports patient percentages; numerators for dizziness and placebo urinary tract infection are not printed.

delivery.label: Post-prostatectomy dosing and home treatment
delivery.value: Clinic titration used 125 and 250 micrograms on separate visits, then 500 or 1000 micrograms if needed, delivered with an applicator inserted 3 cm into the distal urethra; 66.3% of post-prostatectomy clinic responders selected 500 or 1000 micrograms. Of 270 randomized post-prostatectomy responders, 243 (90%) completed three months; 126 active and 137 placebo patients reported home treatment. Monthly visits reviewed treatment diaries.
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods and Results, Clinic and Home treatment phases, p 1326; Table 2, p 1327
